info.title: opencode HttpApi
info.description: Experimental HttpApi surface for selected instance routes.

get.description: Return the server identity, connection URLs, paths, and readiness status.

post.description: Create a short-lived, single-use code for a /auth/connect/:code pairing link.

Redeem a pairing code with an explicit state-changing request. Browsers land on GET first (which never consumes the code) and confirm here; requests that accept JSON receive a session token to use as the password.

get.description: Redeem a pairing code. Browsers receive a session cookie and a redirect to the web app; requests that accept JSON receive a session token to use as the password.
Resolve the requested location or the server default location.

post.description: Shut down and rebuild every loaded location. Pending permissions and forms are cancelled; running sessions continue with fresh services at the next step boundary. Emits location.shutdown for client recovery and responds once all replacement builds settle.

get.description: Retrieve currently registered agents.
Retrieve a single currently registered agent.
Retrieve enabled server plugins and their current status.

Read an active plugin's prebuilt CommonJS `./gui-experimental` bundle. Desktop app windows run its default export; the desktop app's main process runs its `main` export. Fails with not found when no active plugin has the id or the plugin exports no `./gui-experimental`.

post.description: Check one or all package plugins for available updates.
Update package plugins concurrently and notify active locations to reload them. Responds once every update has finished; fails when any update fails.

schema.description: Maximum number of sessions to return, at most 200. Defaults to the newest 50 sessions.
Session order for the first page. Use desc for newest first or asc for oldest first.
Filter by parent session. Use null to return only root sessions.

get.description: Retrieve sessions in the requested order. Items keep that order across pages; use cursor.next or cursor.previous to move through the ordered list.

post.description: Create a session at the requested location. The location payload takes precedence over the directory query parameter, which names the root session's directory; directory cannot be combined with a parentID, because a parentID creates a linked child session at its parent's location. Detached sessions have no interactive question tool, and their child sessions inherit detached mode.

parentID.description: Set parentID to create a subagent session at the parent's location; set agent to choose its agent (otherwise it uses the default) and start it with session.prompt. After each completed round, the child sends a `<background-result kind="subagent">` report to the parent's inbox and wakes the parent unless it has a staged revert.

detached.description: Run in detached (non-interactive) mode. The question tool is unavailable, and every child session inherits this mode.

get.description: Aggregate local session activity, usage, and tool reliability for a time range.

post.description: Import a projected session transcript at the requested location. Accepts transcripts exported by earlier releases. If parentID is supplied, the parent session must already exist; import parents before children.

get.description: Export a complete projected session transcript.
Retrieve foreground Session drains currently owned by this OpenCode process. Sessions absent from the result are inactive.
Retrieve a session by ID.

delete.description: Delete a session and its child sessions.

archived.description: Archive the session with true or restore it with false. Repeating the current state is a no-op.

archivedAt.description: Experimental: may change without compatibility guarantees. Epoch-millisecond archive time for archived: true, for a session a client archived before carrying it over; ignored otherwise. Omitted means now.

post.description: Create a child session by copying projected history before a message. Omit before to copy the full history.
Switch the agent used by subsequent provider turns.
Switch the model used by subsequent provider turns.

get.description: The pool members this session has pinned, one per model pool (opencode-route/<routeID>). Pins live in server memory and are cleared by a restart.

post.description: Pin the session's preferred member of a model pool, or clear the pin with target null, and return the session's pins. The session stays on the pool: the pinned member serves every request while it is healthy, requests fail over to the other members when it errors or is benched, avoided, over budget or quota-demoted, and return to it once it is healthy again. Applies from the next model request. A routeID that names no pool, or a target that is not a member of it, is rejected. Pins live in server memory and are cleared by a restart; other sessions are unaffected.
Move a session to another project directory at the requested delivery boundary.
Durably admit one session input and schedule agent-loop execution unless resume is false.
Execute a slash command callback immediately.
Activate a skill for a session by appending a skill message and resuming execution.
Durably admit synthetic session input and schedule execution unless resume is false.
Execute one shell command in the session's working directory. Emits a shell.started event before execution and a shell.ended event with the merged output after.
Durably admit a session compaction request. Steers by default: it runs at the next step boundary instead of waiting behind queued prompts.
Wait for a session agent loop to become idle.
Stage or move a reversible session boundary and optionally apply its file changes.

get.description: Retrieve the active context messages for a session (all messages after the last compaction).

schema.description: User message whose turn to diff. Defaults to the turn of the newest user message.
Later user message whose turn ends the range. Defaults to the turn of `from` alone.
Unchanged lines around each hunk. Omit for full-file patches.

get.description: Structured per-file diffs of the files a turn changed. A turn runs from the first prompt after the session was last idle until its next idle marker, so prompts steered in while it was busy belong to the same turn; `to` extends the range through a later turn. Compares the range's first recorded snapshot with its last; a step still running in the active session compares against the working copy. Ranges that span a location change are rejected. In sessions without any idle marker, a prompt's turn spans until the next user message.
List durable enqueued session work not yet delivered, ordered by enqueue sequence. Includes user, synthetic, compaction, and move items.

delete.description: Cancel an inbox item that has not yet been delivered. Unknown or already-settled items conflict (409), matching steer/queue.

patch.description: Change a pending inbox item's delivery mode. Steering wakes session execution.

get.description: List API-managed instruction entries attached to the session.

put.description: Attach or replace one durable instruction entry. Changes announce as updates at the next step boundary.

delete.description: Remove one instruction entry; the removal is announced to the model at the next step boundary.

post.description: Generate transient text from the current session context without mutating session history. Its tokens and cost count toward the session's totals.

get.description: Experimental durable session event log. Reads events after an exclusive aggregate sequence and continues with live events when follow=true.

post.description: Interrupt active execution owned by this OpenCode process. Stops cascade background subagents; independent and detached children keep running. When force=true, stops everything under the session regardless of stop policy. Returns interrupted=true when an active execution was interrupted and false for the idle no-op. When resume=true, execution resumes pending steering input and next-in-line control items (manual compaction, moves) while queued prompts remain parked.
Move active foreground backgroundable tools for this session into background observation. Idle requests are a no-op.

get.description: Retrieve one projected message owned by the Session.
Retrieve pending forms for a session.

post.description: Create a form for a session.

get.description: Retrieve a form and its current state for a session.

delete.description: Cancel a pending form, optionally telling the asker why it was not answered.

post.description: Submit an answer to a pending form.

put.description: Replace the process environment used by local shell commands for this session.

post.description: Mark the idle transition observed by the viewer as viewed.

schema.description: Maximum number of messages to return. When omitted, the endpoint returns its default page size.
Message order for the first page. Use desc for newest first or asc for oldest first.
Opaque pagination cursor returned as cursor.previous or cursor.next in the previous response. Do not combine with order.
Filter by message type before pagination. When omitted, all message types are returned. Pass the same type when following cursors.

get.description: Retrieve projected messages for a session, optionally filtered by type. Items keep the requested order across pages; use cursor.next or cursor.previous to move through the ordered timeline, passing the same type filter on each page.

schema.description: Only list models of these types. Defaults to chat, the only type offered for sessions.

get.description: Retrieve the current snapshot of available models of the requested types, chat by default, ordered by release date within each type. The snapshot may precede initial plugin settlement.
Retrieve the model used when a session has no explicit model selection.

post.description: Run one stateless model generation using the server's base configuration and return the assistant text. Uses the base configuration's default model when none is specified.
Deprecated alias of POST /api/experimental/generate/text.
Generate or edit images with an image model using the server's base configuration and return them as base64. Stateless: nothing is stored.

Submit a video job to a video model using the server's base configuration and return its ID once the provider accepted it. The server polls the job and stores the finished videos as blobs; read the job with GET /api/experimental/generate/video/:id and the video with GET /api/experimental/blob/:id. Experimental: may change without compatibility guarantees.

get.description: Read a video job: running, completed with its videos' blobs, or error with a reason. Jobs survive a server restart, which resumes polling running ones. A job is not found 24 hours after it finished, or once none of its blobs remain. Experimental: may change without compatibility guarantees.

post.description: Ask a decision model typed predicate, choice and score questions about the input and return one probability-bearing answer per question, in question order. Stateless: nothing is stored.

Run one stateless chat completion for an external harness. The model is a route reference (opencode-route/workhorse or a bare route id) resolved in-process through the server's own route and provider resolution; no session is created or stored. Answers in the OpenAI chat-completions wire format, streamed as SSE when the payload asks for it.

The universal door in the Responses dialect: the same models the completions endpoint serves — route references and direct catalog provider/model refs — resolved in-process through the server's own route and provider resolution; no session is created or stored. Responses are retained in the façade's private item store, so callers chain with previous_response_id (bounded at 64 links, 24h TTL; an expired or unknown id answers 404 response_not_found). Answers in the OpenAI Responses wire format, streamed as typed SSE events when the payload asks for it.

Embed text with a registered embedding model. The model is a catalog ref (local-embed/snowflake-arctic-embed-m-v2.0, the first registered backend — a local Snowflake Arctic Embed model run in-process by the native ONNX backend) or a bare embedding model id, resolved in-process against the embedding catalog; each registered model carries its own dimension and supported dimensions values, and an unsupported dimensions request is rejected. Input arrays pass through faithfully (varied lengths, no truncation at this layer). Answers in the OpenAI embeddings wire format; every call records a route_attempt row with session_id NULL like the other doors.

Transcribe audio with a registered transcription model (design specs/2026-11-08_design_voice-input-stt-facade.md §2). The request is multipart/form-data with OpenAI-compatible fields; the model is a concrete catalog ref (openai/whisper-1, the first registered backend) resolved in-process against the transcription registry, gated by the same provider config as chat. Batch only in phase 1: stream=true fails typed, never fake-streams. Answers in the normalized §2.3 envelope with §2.4 typed errors; every attempt records a route_attempt row with session_id NULL like the other doors. The payload schema here is nominal — the handler reads the multipart form itself.

The universal door in the Anthropic Messages dialect: the same models the other doors serve — route references and direct catalog provider/model refs — resolved in-process through the server's own route and provider resolution; no session is created or stored. Answers in the Anthropic Messages wire format, streamed as typed SSE events (message_start, content_block_*, message_delta, message_stop) when the payload asks for it. Server authorization is the server's own, as on the other doors; no Anthropic-style x-api-key handling is added.

The systemone-standard door for decision-model JSON traffic (#1410): state + typed questions in, probabilities out, never text. Reproduces the standalone clef proxy's caller-visible contract exactly — the plain {error} envelope, the Clef model grammar, the {answers} success shape — so existing systemone clients (OpenChamber's Jev classifier client, clef callers) repoint with no contract change. Routed to the Cloudflare AI gateway Workers AI run endpoint for the Clef family through the fork's read-in-place credential resolution (caller Bearer, then env, then the Cloudflare config files). No session is created or stored; every attempt records a route_attempt row with session_id NULL like the other doors.
post.summary: Evaluate a System One decision request (systemone-standard)

get.description: The models the completions door serves, in the OpenAI models-list wire format: one entry per configured model route (derived from the Location's model_routes, #1413), the systemone family's Clef floor, and the registered embedding models.

The single model the completions door serves under the given id — a route reference (opencode-route/workhorse, or the bare route id from the models list) or a concrete catalog provider/model ref — in the same shape as a models-list entry. Unknown ids answer 404 in the OpenAI error shape.

The single model the completions door serves under the given provider/model ref — a route reference (opencode-route/workhorse) or a concrete catalog ref (deepseek/deepseek-chat) — in the same shape as a models-list entry. Unknown ids answer 404 in the OpenAI error shape.
get.summary: Get a completion model by provider/model ref (OpenAI-compatible)

get.description: List supported voice models, their transports, and whether the server has a usable API key for each provider.

post.description: Create a server-brokered voice session using the server's configured provider credentials and return the WebRTC SDP answer or WebSocket ephemeral token.

get.description: Retrieve active AI providers, each with its resolved models, so clients can show provider availability and configuration and discover models per provider.
Retrieve a single AI provider with its resolved models so clients can inspect its availability, endpoint settings, and model catalog.
Retrieve available integrations and their authentication methods.
Retrieve one integration and its authentication methods.

post.description: Discover and persist an experimental wellknown integration source.
Run a key authentication method and store the resulting credential.
Run an external authentication method and store a reference to its credential source.
Start an OAuth attempt and return the authorization details.

delete.description: Cancel an OAuth attempt and release its resources.

post.description: Complete a code-based OAuth attempt and store the resulting credential. For an automatic attempt with `paste`, `code` is the redirect URL copied from the browser, and the result arrives through the attempt status.
Start a command authentication attempt.

delete.description: Stop an MCP server and remove it from the runtime set until restart.

get.description: Upgrade to a WebSocket over which the client hosts an MCP server named after `name`; its tools stay available while the socket is open. One JSON-RPC message per text frame. Experimental: may change without compatibility guarantees.
List every stored integration credential, including its secret value.

post.description: Store an integration credential. It becomes the integration's active credential unless activate is false and the integration already has one. Fails with a conflict when the requested ID already exists, and with an invalid request when an `integration.connect` policy denies the integration.
Activate a stored integration credential.

get.description: List the model route overrides currently in force, exactly as routing sees them. The overrides live in the server's own store (route-overrides.json in its data directory); this API is the server-owned surface OpenChamber's duplicate store is being consolidated onto (#2491).

The entry is validated by the same parse routing applies when it reads the store: a malformed entry (no expiry and no schedule, or no provider or model named) is rejected and nothing is stored.

get.description: List known projects. Archived projects are excluded unless archived=true.

patch.description: Update the project canonical directory, display metadata, and workspace commands.

get.description: Retrieve pending forms for a location.
Retrieve pending permission requests for a location.
Retrieve saved permissions, optionally filtered by project.

delete.description: Remove a saved permission by ID.

post.description: Evaluate and, when approval is required, create a permission request for a session.

get.description: Retrieve pending permission requests owned by a session.
Retrieve a pending permission request owned by a session.

get.description: Stream one file relative to the requested location with ETag, Last-Modified, and single-range HTTP Range support (206 Partial Content, 416 Range Not Satisfiable, and 304 Not Modified; multi-range and malformed Range headers fall back to 200).

schema.description: An absolute path or a path relative to the requested location. Defaults to the location directory.

Bodies over 10 MiB are rejected with 413 before any directory or file is created. Unlike read, the target is not confined to the location. Experimental: may change without compatibility guarantees.

Watch one file relative to the requested location for 24 hours, publishing filesystem.changed on that location when it changes. Watching an already watched file resets its expiry. Paths follow read confinement. Experimental: may change without compatibility guarantees.

path.description: A file path relative to the requested location.

schema.description: Only send events of these types, plus the initial server.connected event. When omitted, all events are sent.

get.description: Subscribe to native events and plugin RPC events across all server locations. Each frame carries an SSE id of the form `<instance>:<sequence>`. Reconnect with Last-Event-ID to receive the events after that id from the server's bounded in-process buffer. When the id belongs to another server process or has aged out of the buffer, the stream sends one server.resync event instead, and the client should refetch its state. Otherwise events are volatile: a slow consumer overflows and fails the stream.
List PTY sessions for a location, including exited sessions retained until removal.

Read the last physical rows without changing selection or taking control. Omitted lines uses the live terminal height; larger counts include retained history. Blank rows are preserved. Screen dimensions and cursor remain relative to the live screen. Returns null when no current terminal exists. Selection is server-local and resets on restart. Experimental: may change without compatibility guarantees.

get.description: Stream persistent PTY output through the OpenCode server.

Read a content-addressed media blob by SHA-256 hash with immutable Cache-Control, ETag, and 304 Not Modified support. Only blobs a stored message or inbox item still references are served. Experimental: may change without compatibility guarantees.

Stream a stored blob's bytes, such as a generated video, with single byte Range, ETag and 304 Not Modified support. Blobs are kept until removed. Experimental: may change without compatibility guarantees.

post.description: Create an automation that sends a prompt, runs a Code Mode program, or runs a shell command at a time, every interval, or on a cron. Creating an MCP event watch requires the automation_create tool in a local session; a session ID over HTTP is not a watch authorization. Experimental: may change without compatibility guarantees. get.description: Upgrade to a WebSocket that carries a machine's link to this server: binary messages only, each at most 65,535 bytes. It takes no server password. The link's own handshake, which starts with the machine's first message, is the only way in: it admits a key this server has paired or a valid join string, and closes the socket on anything else without saying why. Behind the machines flag; without it the route does not exist. Experimental: may change without compatibility guarantees.

schema.description: Absolute server-local directory to write the snapshot into, created when missing. Defaults to the server's log directory.

memory.description: The server process's memory in bytes, read just before the snapshot (Node's process.memoryUsage()). rss covers native memory the snapshot cannot show.

Pauses the server while the heap serializes and can temporarily increase its memory use. The snapshot can contain credentials, prompts, and file contents.

Return the registered web search providers.

patch.description: Patch supported fields in the highest-precedence global configuration document.

Automation.ActionInput.description: What it does: { type: "prompt", prompt, to? } sends a prompt; { type: "code", code, args? } runs Code Mode; { type: "shell", command } runs a fixed shell command.

code.description: Code Mode JavaScript run on each trigger with no model (32 KB output cap). Call tools statically as tools.<ns>.<tool>(...) or tools["ns-name"].tool(...); each is authorized once at creation to run unattended. Receives input = { state, now, runs, args } (also globals): state starts null, now is epoch ms, runs counts earlier runs. Event triggers also receive input.event = { id, timestamp, data }; data follows the event type's payloadSchema. Return nothing, or { state?, done?, send? }. JSON state is kept for the next run; done: true stops. lastOutput shows the delivery target and any logs. Return at most one send per run. { send: { prompt } } steers the creating session; { send: { prompt, to: { subagent } } } starts a permitted child that does not report back. No session IDs. Omit send to stay quiet. A rejected send commits neither state nor done. Example code string: if (runs < 2) return; return { done: true, send: { prompt: "Three checks elapsed. Review the build." } }

directory.description: Where it runs when there is no Session. Defaults to the server user's home folder.

name.description: A short label shown in lists.

Automation.Duration.description: A duration such as "90 seconds", "5 minutes" or "2 hours".

prompt.description: The message the target Session receives, with enough context to act on it without this conversation.

command.description: The fixed shell command to run on each trigger without a model.

Automation.Trigger.description: When it runs: { type: "at", at: "in 20 minutes" | "2026-10-27T09:00" }, { type: "every", every: "1 hour" } or { type: "cron", cron: "0 9 * * 1-5" }, each with an optional tz. Or { type: "event", server, event, args? } for a connected MCP server advertising push delivery.

at.description: An instant with an offset, a wall-clock time in tz such as "2026-10-27T09:00", or "in 10 minutes".

Blob.ID.description: A stored blob, such as a generated video, which outlives the job that made it

shell.description: Default shell to use for terminal and shell tool execution

default_agent.description: Default primary agent to use when no session agent is selected

update.description: Disable updates, notify when one is available, or install updates automatically

share.description: Control whether sessions may be shared manually, automatically, or not at all

username.description: Username displayed in conversations and used for telemetry identity

timezone.description: IANA time zone for schedules, e.g. America/Los_Angeles. Defaults to the server's local zone

automations.description: Run prompts, shell commands or Code Mode actions on a timer, on a cron schedule, or on push events from connected MCP servers. Defaults to true; set false to disable.

policies.description: Ordered policies controlling access to providers, tools, and integrations

agents.description: Named built-in agent overrides and custom agent definitions

snapshots.description: Enable snapshots used for undo and revert behavior

formatter.description: Enable built-in formatters or configure formatter overrides

lsp.description: Enable built-in language servers or configure server overrides

startup.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to establish and initialize the MCP server. At most 2147483647 (~24.8 days); a larger value is rejected.

catalog.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for MCP discovery requests such as tools/list and prompts/list. At most 2147483647 (~24.8 days); a larger value is rejected.

execution.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for MCP tool and prompt execution. At most 2147483647 (~24.8 days); a larger value is rejected.

skills.description: Additional paths or URLs to discover skills from

instructions.description: Additional paths or URLs supplying ambient instructions

references.description: Named local directories or Git repositories available as external context

plugins.description: Ordered plugin enablement directives and external package declarations

warming.description: Keep recently active sessions warm with transient model requests (default: false)

presets.description: Topic presets: name to template, overriding or extending the built-in presets

vars.description: Template variables: name to value or template, overriding or extending the built-in variables

session_start.description: Template added to every session's instructions when it starts (default: the current date, time and timezone). An empty string disables it

user.description: Whether the root session sees messages sent to the user (default: "visible")

delivery.description: Default delivery of messages into sessions

match.description: Default match mode for message and log searches (default: "hybrid")

model.description: Fast model (provider/model) that reranks advanced searches; defaults to the session provider's small model

embedding.description: Local embedding model: a tier name ("tiny", "default", "step-up", "top", "off") or detailed settings

providers.description: Provider aliases mapping alias -> providerID, e.g. { ds: 'deepseek' }

models.description: Model aliases. Bare key = global alias -> provider/model[#variant]. Scoped key = provider/key -> model[#variant].

variants.description: Variant/effort aliases. Keys can be bare 'alias', or 'provider/*#alias', '*/model#alias', or 'provider/model#alias'.

providers.description: Provider aliases mapping alias -> providerID, e.g. { ds: 'deepseek' }

models.description: Model aliases. Bare key = global alias -> provider/model[#variant]. Scoped key = provider/key -> model[#variant].

variants.description: Variant/effort aliases. Keys can be bare 'alias', or 'provider/*#alias', '*/model#alias', or 'provider/model#alias'.

portable_shell_scanner.description: Deprecated: the built-in shell permission scanner is now always enabled.

subagent_depth.description: Maximum subagent nesting depth below a top-level session. 0 disables subagents and 1 stops subagents from launching their own. Defaults to 5.

shell_timeout.description: Default timeout in milliseconds for foreground shell commands. 0 disables the timeout. Defaults to 120000.

policies.description: Deprecated: use top-level policies. Ordered policies controlling access to configured resources

threshold.description: Quota failures within the window that demote a route target. Capped at 50, the number of quota events retained per target, so a threshold can never be set beyond what is counted. Defaults to 3.

window_ms.description: How long a quota failure counts toward demotion, in milliseconds. Defaults to 14400000 (4h).

schedules.description: Time-bound weight changes across routes: during a local-time window, matching provider/model targets are ranked higher or lower (or given a fixed weight) on every route they appear on. Weights order every selection mode; equal weights keep their configured order.

enabled.description: Review routing history on a schedule and put the resulting adjustments in force without asking, for every route that uses rules as well as those at adaptive or higher. They only lower a target's share or skip it, and lapse on their own. Defaults to false.

windowHours.description: How much history each review looks at. Defaults to 24.

notes.description: What the history cannot say, one note per line as `match: text`, where `match` is a case-insensitive substring of provider/model. A text that states when a limit returns, such as `reset at 2026-01-01` or `back in 3 hours`, skips the matching targets until then. The rest is shown to the agent by route_stats.

captureErrorBodies.description: Keep the first 2 KB of a failed request's error body in the routing history, with credentials redacted. A provider body can echo the request, so this is off by default. Defaults to false.

maxCooldownMs.description: The longest bench any failure can impose, however far the ladder escalates. Defaults to 86400000 (24h).

multiplier.description: Each consecutive failure multiplies the bench by this. 1 keeps every bench at its base. Defaults to 2.

failureCapMs.description: The longest bench an ordinary failure (transport, provider-internal, unclassified) can impose, however far its consecutive-failure ladder escalates: the leg gets this short grace and the route moves on. Quota and authentication benches are not bounded by it. Defaults to 120000.

retryAfterMinMs.description: A provider's stated retry-after is believed, but never as less than this. Defaults to 1000.

cooldownCapMs.description: Caps a route health block's failure cooldown (cooldownMs). Defaults to 3600000 (1h).

quotaCooldownCapMs.description: Caps a route health block's quota cooldown (quotaCooldownMs). Defaults to 86400000 (24h).

after.description: Quota errors within the window that demote a target. Capped at 50, the number of quota events retained per target, so a threshold can never be set beyond what is counted. Defaults to 3.

windowMs.description: How long a quota error counts toward demotion. Defaults to 14400000 (4h).

factor.description: A demoted target's weight is multiplied by this. Defaults to 0.01.

maxMs.description: The longest a single exhaustion reading may hold a gate: a stated reset further out than this is capped rather than believed. Defaults to 2592000000 (30 days).

fallbackMs.description: The hold when an exhaustion reading states no usable reset: long enough to stop a 429 on every turn, short enough that a recovered pool is retried promptly. Defaults to 1800000 (30 minutes).

feedTtlMs.description: How often quota snapshots are fed into the gate. Defaults to 60000.

balanceDeadThreshold.description: A credit balance at or below this USD amount is treated as exhausted. Defaults to 0.1.

rootStartMaxPct.description: A new root session is not started on a pool at or above this percent of a quota window; subsessions may be placed up to 100%. Defaults to 85.

rootStartEnabled.description: Whether the root-start gate is applied in placement. When false, new root sessions are placed without regard to rootStartMaxPct (the known-full quota gate still applies). Defaults to true.

enabled.description: Whether routes race their next target once the current one keeps giving up. Defaults to true.

afterGiveUps.description: Give-ups among a target's recent outcomes that mark it unsteady and start escalation. Cannot exceed the outcome window, because the count reads only the retained outcomes in that window. Defaults to 2.

outcomeWindow.description: Recent finished requests per target that the give-up count reads. Defaults to 5.

windowMs.description: The window recent transport failures are compared within. Defaults to 30000.

providers.description: Unrelated providers failing within the window that mark the fault as the local network. At least 2: a single provider failing is that provider's fault. Defaults to 3.

providerModels.description: Models of one provider cooling at once that demote the provider itself to last resort. Defaults to 2.

waitMs.description: The longest a request waits for a membership slot to free before failing over to the next leg. The wait is bounded so it can never hold a session on a capped leg; when the bound expires the request moves on. Defaults to 5000.

hedgeRequests.description: Requests a session that just failed over may hedge back to its origin for. Defaults to 2.

preferredFactor.description: How much a user's "prefer" lifts a target when they don't say by how much. Defaults to 3.

url.description: GGUF download URL used instead of the tier's model

sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 of the custom GGUF file; verified after download when set

size.description: Expected size in bytes of the custom GGUF file; bounds the download exactly when set

path.description: Existing local GGUF file used instead of downloading

pooling.description: Pooling override (default: the tier's pooling; for a custom model, last for Qwen3 embedding files and mean otherwise)

query.description: Instruction prefix for search queries, replacing the tier's prefix; the remote endpoint uses it too

server.description: llama-server executable to use instead of the downloaded llama.cpp build

autostart.description: Download and start the model in the background at startup (default: true)

gpu_layers.description: Layers to offload to the GPU (default: all)

url.description: Base URL of an OpenAI-compatible API, for example https://api.openai.com/v1

key.description: API key; {env:NAME} reads it from the environment

releaseDate.description: Release date as YYYY-MM-DD or YYYY-MM

defaultVariant.description: The variant (effort) a request runs at when it names none or asks for the default, e.g. high. A request that names a variant still runs at it unless lockVariant is set. Ignored when the model does not offer the variant.

lockVariant.description: Run every request at defaultVariant, whatever variant it names, including inside model routes. Has no effect without defaultVariant.

softLimit.description: Fraction of an allowance at which the target is passed over. Defaults to 0.9.

providers.description: Provider IDs the change covers, compared case-insensitively.

models.description: Model ID patterns the change covers, `*` allowed, e.g. ["*flash*"].

routes.description: Route IDs the change is limited to, including nested ones, matched in any case. Empty or unset means every route.

when.description: When the change is in force: a window object, or the name of a window from experimental.routes.windows. An unknown name drops the rule.

factor.description: Multiplies the target's configured weight while the window is active.

weight.description: Sets the target's weight outright while the window is active, instead of scaling it.

providers.description: Member provider ids, in configured order. Members must be concrete providers: a provider route cannot name another provider route (no nesting), and the routes provider is not a member. A member that names no known provider contributes no leaves.

selection.description: How the serving member is picked for a model: ordered uses the first ready member, round-robin rotates per session (a weight is a priority tier there), weighted draws by weights. The choice is sticky per session and failover falls through the remaining members in order - the model-route selection modes, at provider level. Defaults to ordered.

weights.description: Relative weights keyed by member provider id, e.g. { "openai.alternate": 2, "openai": 1 }. Members without a weight count as 1. In a round-robin provider route a weight is a priority tier; in a weighted one it is a relative ratio; in an ordered one weights rank the failover order.

windows.description: Per-member eligibility gates keyed by member provider id: the name of a window defined in experimental.routes.windows, or { "name": ..., "invert": true }. A member is a candidate only while its named window is active (or, inverted, only while it is not) — the provider-granularity counterpart of a model-route target's `window` gate, so a provider can be benched by the clock wherever it participates: as a model-route leaf or as a provider-route member (#1140). An unknown window name drops the gate, leaving the member always eligible.

schedules.description: Time-bound weight changes for this provider route's members, in the same shape as a model route's schedules: `targets` are `provider/model` patterns (`*` allowed), so a rule can name a provider (`openai/*`), a model (`*/gpt-6-*`), a provider/model pair, or every member (empty targets). The rules apply to the concrete leaves the provider route expands to, exactly as a model route's schedules apply to its targets.

Config.ModelRoute.ProviderRoutes.description: Provider routes: named selections over concrete providers (ordered, round-robin, or weighted). A route target names one exactly like a concrete provider — `openai-plan/gpt-6.1-terra` — and resolution picks the member that serves the model, so a provider-level order is defined once instead of once per model.

Config.ModelRoute.ProviderRoutes_1.description: Deprecated: use experimental.routes.providers. Provider routes: named selections over concrete providers (ordered, round-robin, or weighted). A route target names one exactly like a concrete provider — `openai-plan/gpt-6.1-terra` — and resolution picks the member that serves the model, so a provider-level order is defined once instead of once per model.

system.description: System prompt this route carries, prepended to the caller's own system text on every request the route serves (persona routes, #1413: the design-code door's injected design prompt, carried by the route instead of a proxy). A route nested inside another route does not stack its prompt: only the addressed route's prompt applies.

class.description: The route's cost/capability class, e.g. "frontier" or "frontier-acp". When a session's whole route is walled, failover may substitute another route of the SAME class, ordered by the doors' measured record; it never substitutes across classes, so a session never lands on a more expensive or differently-capable route by failing over. A route with no class neither substitutes nor is substituted into. ACP routes are their own class: name them separately (e.g. "frontier-acp") so ACP traffic only ever substitutes within ACP. Class names match in any case.

targets.description: Ordered provider/model references. A route may include another route reference. A * in the model matches within that one provider and is case-sensitive. Optional when include, contains or match supply the models.

include.description: Patterns whose models join the route after its targets, in provider order. Only models of connected providers are matched, so connecting a provider adds its matching models. * matches any run of characters, re: starts a regular expression, and case never matters. A pattern with / is tested against provider/model, one without against the model id in every provider. A route name, or opencode-route/<name>, in any case, stands for that route's models. E.g. ["*luna*", "anthropic/*haiku*", "small"].

exclude.description: Patterns, written as in include, whose models are removed from the route, including those its targets and nested routes bring. E.g. ["*-mini", "frontier-direct"].

contains.description: Text whose models join the route: found anywhere in provider/model, so a provider id matches too. Case never matters, and only models of connected providers are matched. E.g. ["haiku", "sonnet", "opus"].

notContains.description: Text, written as in contains, whose models are removed from the route.

match.description: One expression whose models join the route: patterns and route names joined by and, or, not and parentheses, e.g. "(*luna* or *haiku*) and not *-mini". Quote a term that has spaces or parentheses, such as 're:gpt-(5|6)$'. There is no xor.

levels.description: The levels (variants) the route offers, e.g. ["low", "medium", "high"]. Each target runs a level through its remap, else its own variant of that name, else sits the level out. A level no target can run is left out and logged. Nested in another route, the route keeps its levels: its members sit out every other level. Unset, the route offers each level that at least one target runs and every other target runs or sits out, and none when a target is pinned with #variant.

variantRules.description: Level remaps for the route's models chosen by pattern, applied in order. They reach models of nested routes too, where the nested route's own rules come later. A target's own variants override them. A route nested as opencode-route/<id>#<level> runs only at that level, so its rules decide only whether a member sits that level out.

firstTokenTimeoutMs.description: Fail over if the target produces no response output within this many milliseconds. Defaults to 30000; a route that nests other routes defaults to the longest wait among them (see nestedTimeout). false waits without a limit.

lastTargetTimeoutMs.description: How long the last target that can take the request may go without response output. firstTokenTimeoutMs only moves a request to another target, so once it passes with no other target left, the target keeps going until this many milliseconds instead of failing. Defaults to 900000 (15 minutes), the silence OpenCode allows any streaming response. A value at or below firstTokenTimeoutMs ends the last target at firstTokenTimeoutMs; false waits without a limit.

maxResponseTimeMs.description: Count a completed response as slow when it exceeds this many milliseconds, measured to the end of the model's response. Tools that the step runs afterwards do not count.

minOutputTokensPerSecond.description: Count a completed response as slow when output throughput, from the model's first output to the end of its response, falls below this rate.

sampleWindow.description: Number of completed requests in the rolling performance window. Defaults to 5.

slowThreshold.description: Slow requests in the window that mark a target degraded. Defaults to 3.

cooldownMs.description: How long a failed or degraded target is skipped. Defaults to 60000.

quotaCooldownMs.description: How long a target is skipped after the provider reports an exhausted quota without saying when it resets. A reported retry-after always wins. Defaults to 900000.

nestedTimeout.description: How a route that nests other routes (as opencode-route/<id> targets, or by name in include or match) waits for first output. longest (the default when health.firstTokenTimeoutMs is unset) and shortest take the longest or shortest wait of the nested routes and apply it to every target, replacing health.firstTokenTimeoutMs. own keeps health.firstTokenTimeoutMs for the route's own targets and lets each nested route's targets wait as long as that nested route would. Has no effect on a route that nests none.

budgets.description: Allowances keyed by target model reference, e.g. { "openai/gpt-6-luna": { "requestsPerDay": 500, "tokensPerMinute": 200000 } }. Usage is counted from every request OpenCode makes to the target and is restored from history after a restart.

hedgeAfterMs.description: Send the same request to the next target when the current one has produced no output after this many milliseconds. The first to answer wins and the other is cancelled; nothing is shown or run before a winner is known. Costs a duplicate request whenever the first target is slow. Off by default.

attempts.description: Total requests to make against one target before failing over to the next, so 2 allows one retry. Defaults to 2. Retries only happen before any response output, so no tool call ever runs twice.

autonomy.description: How much the route may decide for itself; each level includes the ones before it. fixed: failover only, starting from the configured order; schedules, the user's prefer and avoid rules and quota demotion still apply. rules: adds selection modes, weights, budgets and provider rate-limit holds. adaptive: adds the scheduled review that skips or down-weights targets from recent history. predictive: adds time-of-day and error-text prediction. agent: adds route_stats and route_adjust so the model can inspect and steer routing; once any route is agent or unset, every session gets them, and they cover every route. Unset keeps the behavior from before levels existed.

selection.description: How a session picks its target: ordered (default) takes the heaviest ready target, in configured order when weights are equal; round-robin rotates per new session in proportion to weight; weighted draws by weight. Either way the choice is sticky for the session, and failover picks again the same way among the targets not yet tried.

weights.description: Relative weights keyed by target model reference. They rank targets in every selection mode, failover included: ordered tries the heaviest first, round-robin rotates in proportion, and weighted draws in proportion, so { "openai/gpt-6-luna": 3, "github-copilot/gpt-6-luna": 1 } sends about 3/4 of new weighted sessions to the first target. Targets without a weight count as 1, and a fixed route ignores weights. A nested route is keyed as "opencode-route/<id>", in any case, and is chosen as one unit by this route; it then picks among its own members using its own selection and weights.

schedules.description: Time-bound weight changes for this route's targets, e.g. peak hours that make a provider lighter. Weights order every selection mode: inside an active window the targets are ranked by effective weight, and equal weights keep their configured order.

context.description: Caps the context limit the route presents, below every target's own limit — e.g. 100000 keeps sessions on this route inside a pricing tier that ends at 100k context, or compacts them earlier than the targets would. The effective limit is the smaller of this cap and the targets' minimum, so a cap can never raise a route above what its targets support.

limit.description: Limits the route presents as its own, regardless of its targets' limits.

id.description: Name for the schedule, shown in decisions and editors.

targets.description: Target references this change covers, `*` allowed, e.g. ["deepseek/*", "openai/gpt-6-*"]. Empty or unset means every target of the route.

when.description: When the change is in force: a window object, or the name of a window from experimental.routes.windows. An unknown name drops the rule.

factor.description: Multiplies the target's configured weight while the window is active. 0.8 makes a weight of 2 become 1.6; 1.2 makes it 2.4. Exactly one of factor and weight is expected.

weight.description: Sets the target's weight outright while the window is active, instead of scaling it. Applied before any user preference for the target.

note.description: Why the schedule exists, kept for review.

exclude.description: Doors (provider ids) excluded from a door-set target (a target whose provider is `*`). Exclusions always win over the door set: an excluded door never contributes a leaf, even when its catalog lists the model. Providers removed by `disabled_providers` never reach expansion at all. Has no effect on a target that names a single provider.

defaultVariant.description: Variant used when the route is selected without an explicit variant. A nested route ignores it.

variants.description: Remaps a route-level variant to this target's variant, e.g. { "low": "high" } runs this target at high when the route is selected at low. false makes the target sit that level out, e.g. { "max": false }: it is never used at that level, not even as a last resort. Overrides the route's variantRules level by level. On a nested route only false applies, and the whole route sits that level out; a string remap, defaultVariant and until are ignored there, with a config warning.

until.description: Epoch milliseconds after which this target leaves the route. Used for time-limited pool membership; takes effect when the configuration reloads. A nested route ignores it.

context.description: Caps the context this target serves within the route, below its own limit — e.g. 100000 keeps this target on requests inside a pricing tier that ends at 100k context. A request that does not fit this ceiling and the route's own cap skips this target like any other ineligible target.

limit.description: Per-target context ceiling within the route; a request that does not fit skips this target.

window.description: Eligibility gate: the name of a window defined in experimental.routes.windows, or { "name": ..., "invert": true }. The target is only in the route while the named window is active, or while it is not active when inverted — e.g. a DeepSeek target gated on the inverse of "deepseek-peak" is a candidate off-peak only, and the same target gated on "deepseek-peak" itself is the peak fallback. An unknown window name drops the gate, leaving the target always eligible.

match.description: Which models the rule covers: a pattern, a route name in any case, or an expression of them with and, or, not and parentheses, as in the route's match, e.g. "*argon*" or "claude and not *haiku*".

map.description: Route-level variant to the variant the model runs it at, or false to sit that level out, e.g. { "xhigh": "high", "max": false }. A later rule overrides an earlier one level by level, and a target's own variants override every rule.

items.description: A weekday as a name (any case, padding ignored) or a number 0 (Sunday) to 6 (Saturday); numeric strings are accepted.

daysOfWeek.description: Weekdays the window is active on. Unset means every day; an empty list is invalid.

items.description: A day of the month, 1 to 31, or -1 for the last day of the month; numeric strings are accepted.

daysOfMonth.description: Days of the month the window is active on. Unset means every day; an empty list is invalid.

dates.description: Specific local calendar dates the window is active on, each "YYYY-MM-DD" or an inclusive range "YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD", read as calendar days in the window's timezone. Unset means every date. Use for one-off days a recurring day list cannot express, such as a holiday calendar defined once as a named window.

excludeDates.description: Local calendar dates the window is never active on, each "YYYY-MM-DD" or an inclusive range "YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD", in the window's timezone. Exclusions win over every other field — e.g. a weekday peak window with the provider's public holidays here stays off on those holidays.

excludeWindows.description: Names of windows defined in experimental.routes.windows; while any named window is active, this window is not. A named window that is only a list of dates is a reusable holiday calendar shared by many windows. An unknown name or a reference cycle drops this window rather than applying it without its exclusion. An empty list is invalid.

start.description: Local start of the daily window as "HH:mm". Unset means from the start of the day. A start later than the end runs past midnight into the following morning.

end.description: Local end of the daily window as "HH:mm", exclusive. Unset means to the end of the day.

timezone.description: IANA timezone such as "America/Chicago". Unset means the host's local timezone.

from.description: Epoch milliseconds before which the window never applies.

until.description: Epoch milliseconds after which the window never applies.

Config.ModelRoute.Windows.description: Named, reusable time windows for route rules, keyed by name, e.g. "deepseek-peak": weekdays 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC. Schedules reference a window by name instead of repeating it, and a route target can gate its eligibility on one: the target is a candidate only while its named window is active (or, inverted, only while it is not). Windows belong to the meter, not the model.

Config.ModelRoute.Windows_1.description: Deprecated: use experimental.routes.windows. Named, reusable time windows for route rules, keyed by name, e.g. "deepseek-peak": weekdays 01:00-04:00 and 06:00-10:00 UTC. Schedules reference a window by name instead of repeating it, and a route target can gate its eligibility on one: the target is a candidate only while its named window is active (or, inverted, only while it is not). Windows belong to the meter, not the model.

Config.ModelRoutes.description: Named ordered provider/model routes with failure and performance failover

Config.ModelRoutes_1.description: Deprecated: use experimental.routes.models. Named ordered provider/model routes with failure and performance failover
